docs.title: Systems Platform and Intelligence Lab
docs.text: This guide covers the sprc GPU cluster for two supported audiences: research-lab members and students using the cluster through a supported course. Both use the same login host, compute nodes, Slurm scheduler, and Sprocket portal, but their accounts are governed differently.

docs.title: Choose your path
docs.text:
• Research account: start with Accounts and access, then Running jobs. Your default research tier, recent usage, and optional deadline or best-effort tiers determine scheduling.
  • Course-only account: start with Course workflow. Your open assignment, GPU-minute budget, holder, deadline, and course capacity schedule determine what you can submit.
  • Researcher enrolled in a course: you keep the research workflow by default. Add the assignment account shown in Sprocket only when the job is course work. Accounts and access explains the boundary.

docs.title: Cluster at a glance
docs.text:
The cluster has four compute nodes, sprc00 through sprc03. Each has two NVIDIA H100 NVL GPUs, 128 schedulable CPUs, and about 1.5 TB of memory. The shared total is eight GPUs.

Connect first to the login host:

ssh <username>@sprlab005.csl.illinois.edu

The login host is for editing, source control, file management, and submitting jobs. GPU work and heavy CPU work belong in Slurm jobs on the compute nodes.

salloc --gres=gpu:1 --time=1:00:00     # short interactive research session
sbatch --gres=gpu:1 --time=12:00:00 train.sh
squeue --me

Course students use the same commands with the assignment account shown on Sprocket’s Checkpoints page. Course-only accounts are automatically kept inside the course policy.

docs.title: What Sprocket provides
docs.text: Sprocket is the cluster portal. It provides live capacity and contention, queue and usage views, service status and announcements, account and storage information, support and resource requests, and course-specific checkpoints, budgets, submissions, and adjustments. See Using the Sprocket portal for the complete map.

docs.title: Shared expectations
docs.text:
• Request only the GPUs, CPUs, memory, and wall time the job needs.
  • Use short interactive sessions to develop and debug; use sbatch for unattended work.
  • Keep heavy work off the login host.
  • Cancel work you no longer need and clean temporary data from shared fast storage.
  • Treat displayed start times as estimates, not guarantees.
  • Use Sprocket Support when something is broken. Course-policy and assignment questions go to course staff; research coordination can also use the lab’s #server channel.

docs.title: Accounts and access
docs.text: Your account type decides which Slurm policy applies. It does not change the hardware you use or the login host you connect to.

docs.title: Before connecting
docs.text:
Sprocket and the login host accept campus traffic. When off campus, connect to the university VPN before opening the portal or using SSH.

ssh <username>@sprlab005.csl.illinois.edu

For most people the cluster username is their NetID. The welcome message is authoritative if a different username was assigned. Use Sprocket’s Me page to review the account and manage SSH keys when that option is available.

docs.title: Account types
docs.text:
Account Intended use Default scheduling behavior Storage Graduate researcher Lab research normal research tier Shared /spr-storage/home plus research storage tiers Undergraduate researcher Lab research undergrad research tier Shared /spr-storage/home plus research storage tiers Course-only student Work for an enrolled course course policy and an open assignment budget Personal /course/<NetID> and, when assigned, a team workspace Researcher enrolled in a course Research and course work Research by default; course only when an assignment account is selected Existing research home, isolated personal coursework storage, and assigned team storage

An undergraduate research account is not the same thing as a course-only student account. The former participates in research fair sharing under undergrad; the latter can run only work authorized by an open course assignment.

docs.title: Research accounts
docs.text:
Research jobs use the account and default QoS installed for the researcher. Graduate researchers default to normal; undergraduate researchers default to undergrad. Do not pass --account for ordinary research work.

Research accounts may opt into scavenger for restartable batch work. A time-limited expedite grant is available for genuine research deadlines. Priority, capacity, and fair sharing has the exact limits.

docs.title: Course-only students
docs.text:
A course-only UID always enters the course gate. It cannot fall through to research QoS, the research debug partition, or unbudgeted CPU-only compute.

Selecting a course during roster invitation creates the student membership and individual holder together with the invite. During acceptance, a new course-only student must add an SSH public key; the account has no usable password. Sprocket then creates the locked Unix identity, private /course/<NetID> home, compute-node identities, SSH key, and Slurm holder before enabling portal access. A failure pauses the durable setup job for an administrator to retry instead of reporting a partially built account as ready.

Course compute requires all of the following:

  1. an active course membership;
  2. at least one open assignment for the student or team;
  3. a fresh budget reading;
  4. enough free GPU-minutes for requested GPUs multiplied by requested wall time; and
  5. a request within the assignment’s GPU and wall-time ceilings.

If no assignment is open or no budget remains, compute access takes a no-budget posture: the account remains present, but no job can be submitted. A later assignment restores access through its own budget.

docs.title: Researchers who are also course students
docs.text:
Dual-role users remain research users unless they explicitly select course work. This keeps an ordinary research command out of course reservations and budgets:

Their existing UID and research passwd home remain authoritative. Course convergence adds a separate /course/<NetID> coursework dataset for individual path snapshots; it does not replace $HOME or create a second identity.

sbatch --gres=gpu:1 --time=4:00:00 research.sh

For course work, use the assignment account displayed on Sprocket:

sbatch --account=<assignment> --gres=gpu:1 --time=1:00:00 course.sh

Selecting a course account applies the full course posture: assignment budget, course QoS, course capacity reservation, one-node limit, and holder GPU cap. Selecting a research account from a course-only UID does not bypass the gate.

docs.title: If access does not work
docs.text:
• Portal sign-in or SSH problem: use Sprocket Support.
  • No course or checkpoint appears: contact course staff; membership and publication are instructor-controlled.
  • Invalid account or account/partition combination: include the exact command and error in a support report.
  • Resource or storage request: use Resource requests. Course budget exceptions follow the adjustment workflow on the Checkpoints page instead.

docs.title: Agentic coding helper
docs.text: The sprc-slurm plugin teaches supported coding agents how to stage, submit, monitor, and debug work on this cluster. It is useful for translating a plain-language request into salloc, sbatch, squeue, and sacct operations.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The plugin ships from the sprc-plugins marketplace.

In Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add platformx-students/sprc-plugins
/plugin install sprc-slurm@sprc-plugins
/reload-plugins

For Codex, ohmypi, or another skills-aware harness, follow the repository’s installation instructions.

docs.title: Useful requests
docs.text:
• “Run train.py on one GPU for six hours and email me when it finishes.”
  • “Why is job 4213 pending?”
  • “Package this as a checkpointing batch job suitable for scavenger.”
  • “Submit this against the course assignment account shown by mybudget for 30 minutes.”

docs.title: Course safety
docs.text:
An agent does not create budget or choose which overlapping assignment should pay. For course work:

  1. inspect Sprocket Checkpoints or run mybudget;
  2. name the intended assignment explicitly;
  3. verify GPUs × requested minutes fits the free budget; and
  4. review the generated command before submission.

The Slurm course gate remains authoritative and fails closed if accounting is unavailable. Never ask an agent to work around an account, QoS, reservation, or budget rejection.

docs.title: Responsibility
docs.text:
The plugin is a convenience, not a separate execution system. Every command runs with the user’s account and permissions. Review destructive commands, requested resources, output paths, and repository changes exactly as you would if typing them yourself.

Use Sprocket Support for plugin or cluster problems and include the generated command and error.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text: Use these commands from sprlab005. See Running jobs for the workflow and Course workflow for assignment budgets.

docs.title: Interactive work
docs.text:
Research account:

salloc --gres=gpu:1 --time=1:00:00
salloc --cpus-per-task=8 --mem=32G --time=1:00:00

Course work:

salloc --account=<assignment> --gres=gpu:1 --time=0:30:00
mybudget

Research interactive work routes to debug and is capped at one hour. Course work routes through its assignment on main; its checkpoint controls the maximum and always requires a GPU.

After the allocation starts:

squeue --me
ssh <assigned-node>
nvidia-smi

docs.title: Batch work
docs.text:
sbatch --gres=gpu:1 --time=12:00:00 train.sh
sbatch --account=<assignment> --gres=gpu:1 --time=1:00:00 course.sh

A batch script can carry the options itself:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --account=<assignment>     # course only; omit for research
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --time=1:00:00
#SBATCH --job-name=train
#SBATCH --mail-type=END,FAIL
#SBATCH --mail-user=<netid>
srun python train.py

docs.title: Watch the cluster
docs.text:
squeue --me
squeue
squeue --me --start
sinfo
sinfo -N -l
scontrol show job <jobid>

Common pending reasons:

Reason Meaning Resources The requested shape is not free. Priority Other pending work is ahead. AssocGrpGRES An account or holder GPU cap is already in use. QOSMaxWallDurationPerJobLimit The requested time exceeds the selected tier. Reservation or ReqNodeNotAvail The job is waiting on an applicable capacity window or node.

Sprocket’s Queue and Usage pages provide a friendlier view.

docs.title: Stop jobs
docs.text:
scancel <jobid>
scancel --me

docs.title: Inspect completed work
docs.text:
sacct -j <jobid>
sacct -u <username> --starttime 2026-08-01
sacct -j <jobid> --format=JobID,State,Elapsed,MaxRSS,ReqTRES,Account
State Meaning COMPLETED Program exited successfully. TIMEOUT Job reached its requested wall time. FAILED Program exited non-zero. OUT_OF_MEMORY Job exceeded requested memory. CANCELLED User or an administrator cancelled the job. PREEMPTED Best-effort work yielded to higher-priority work.

docs.title: Common options
docs.text:
Option Purpose --gres=gpu:N Request whole GPUs. Each node has two. --time=HH:MM:SS Maximum wall time. Request what the job realistically needs. --cpus-per-task=N or -c N Request Slurm CPUs. --mem=32G Request job memory. --account=<assignment> Charge course work to the assignment shown in Sprocket. Do not use for ordinary research. --qos=scavenger Restartable, lowest-priority research batch work. --qos=expedite Research deadline work during an approved grant. --mail-type=END,FAIL Select email events. Also accepts BEGIN, TIME_LIMIT, and ALL. --mail-user=<netid> Deliver to the university address for a bare NetID. --job-name=<name> or -J <name> Give the job a readable name.

Do not normally set a partition. Slurm routes research interactive work to debug, research batch to main, and course work to the appropriate course reservation on main.

docs.title: Course-specific constraints
docs.text:
• Use the assignment account from Checkpoints; it is required when assignments overlap.
  • GPU-minute cost is requested GPUs × requested minutes.
  • CPU-only course jobs and job arrays are rejected.
  • Course jobs use one node and at most two GPUs, 64 CPUs, and 512 GB; a checkpoint may be stricter.
  • Cancel and resubmit to change resource or placement fields on a queued course job.

docs.title: Need help?
docs.text: Use Sprocket Support and include the command, job ID, time, and exact error. Research resource requests go through Resource requests; course budget and deadline exceptions use the adjustment workflow on Checkpoints.

docs.title: Course workflow
docs.text: Course compute is organized around open assignments in Sprocket. Each assignment has its own Slurm account, availability window, GPU-minute budget, GPU cap, wall-time ceiling, storage allowance, and submission rules. Instructors configure those values in the portal.

docs.title: 1. Open the course workspace
docs.text:
Sign in to Sprocket and open Course → Getting started, then Course → Checkpoints. The workspace shows:

  • every published checkpoint and deadline;
  • every assignment currently open to you;
  • the exact --account=<assignment> value to use;
  • total, consumed, held, and free GPU-minutes;
  • whether the holder is you or a team;
  • budget freshness and the effective close time; and
  • declared and confirmed submission revisions.

If more than one assignment is open, choose one explicitly with --account. Even with only one open assignment, copying the displayed account makes scripts unambiguous and reproducible.

docs.title: 2. Understand the budget
docs.text:
One GPU for one minute costs one GPU-minute. Two GPUs for one minute cost two GPU-minutes.

job reservation = requested wall minutes × requested GPUs
free budget     = total budget − consumed minutes − held minutes

Pending and running jobs hold their full requested cost so several submissions cannot overspend the same budget. When a job completes, accounting replaces that hold with its actual elapsed GPU-time. Ask for a realistic wall time: an unnecessarily large request can consume all free headroom while the job is queued or running.

Budgets belong to the assignment holder. An individual assignment has a personal pool; a team assignment has one pool shared by every member. Team members’ jobs all draw from that same pool.

Budgets do not roll into another assignment. Overlapping assignments remain separate pools, while the two-GPU holder ceiling spans them so opening a second assignment does not double concurrency.

Check from either surface:

mybudget                       # shell view

or use the Checkpoints page. If accounting is missing or stale, course submission fails closed rather than running without a limit.

docs.title: 3. Run course work
docs.text:
Course jobs require at least one GPU, run on main, use one compute node, and are attached to the active course capacity reservation. Do not request debug, normal, undergrad, expedite, or scavenger for course work.

# short interactive test
salloc --account=<assignment> --gres=gpu:1 --time=0:30:00

# unattended job
sbatch --account=<assignment> --gres=gpu:1 --time=1:00:00 train.sh

The cluster-wide course ceiling is two GPUs per holder and two GPUs per course user. A checkpoint may set a lower GPU or wall-time limit. Each job is limited to one node, 64 CPUs, and 512 GB of memory. Job arrays are not accepted because every array element would need an independent budget reservation.

After submission, resource-changing edits are rejected because they would invalidate the reserved cost. Cancel and resubmit to change the account, QoS, partition, reservation, GPUs, CPUs, memory, nodes, or wall time. Naming, holding, and releasing a job remain available.

docs.title: 4. Work with a team
docs.text:
When a checkpoint uses team holders, every team member shares its compute budget and team workspace. Coordinate before launching large jobs: another member’s pending job can hold budget even before it starts.

Instructors can correct team membership for drops, reassignments, or other exceptions. A reviewed change can keep, reset, explicitly set, remove, or transfer free budget. Consumed time, time held by existing jobs, closed history, and existing artifacts never move silently. An open submission that no longer matches the team may require a new declaration and confirmation.

docs.title: 5. Store course files
docs.text:
• Course-only students receive a private /course/<NetID> workspace with a 10 GB quota.
  • Team checkpoints can provide a shared 50 GB workspace under /course/groups/<course>/<team>.
  • A researcher enrolled in a course keeps the existing research UID and passwd home. Sprocket also provides an isolated /course/<NetID> personal coursework workspace so individual path revisions can be snapshotted without touching the research home; the team workspace is added for team work.

Exact checkpoint storage allowances may be higher and never reduce a live dataset below its existing usage. Immutable path revisions count against the same storage boundary; obsolete draft revisions are pruned while open and final revisions are retained. Keep another durable copy of important work rather than relying on temporary working storage.

docs.title: 6. Declare and confirm a submission
docs.text:
On Checkpoints, choose a source allowed by the instructor:

  • For Course workspace path, enter an absolute path inside the workspace shown by Sprocket. The portal snapshots that path, rejects links, special files, empty or oversized trees, and immediately shows whether the immutable revision is valid. A checkpoint may also run an instructor-provided Python verifier in a short-lived, read-only, no-network sandbox.
  • For GitHub, enter an owner/repository and a branch, tag, or commit. Sprocket resolves it server-side to an immutable commit.

An invalid declaration never replaces the current valid attempt. Correct the path or repository and create another revision. Review the selected source, validity result, and immutable revision before confirming.

For team submissions, every required team member confirms the same revision. Final confirmation is blocked while jobs are active or job evidence is stale. Once confirmation succeeds, the holder’s assignment window closes immediately and that revision becomes the final submission. If nobody confirms early, the deadline worker selects the latest eligible declaration or records no submission when the effective close time passes.

Confirmation is consequential: stop or finish relevant jobs, verify outputs are pushed, confirm the immutable revision, and only then acknowledge the finalization warning.

docs.title: 7. Extensions and exceptions
docs.text:
Use Request an adjustment on the checkpoint when an exception needs additional GPU-minutes and a later expiry. The form requires an explanation and supporting PDF, JPEG, or PNG no larger than 5 MiB. Evidence is private to the requester and authorized course staff, and downloads are audited.

Course staff may approve or deny the request and may correct a holder’s open or close time. Reopening a finalized checkpoint preserves the earlier outcome and grading record as superseded history; it does not erase them.

For a technical failure, use Sprocket Support. Assignment rules, grading, teams, and deadline decisions belong with course staff.

docs.title: Why did my job stop?
docs.text:
Run:

sacct -j <jobid> --format=JobID,State,Elapsed,MaxRSS,ReqTRES
  • TIMEOUT: the job reached --time.
  • OUT_OF_MEMORY: it exceeded requested memory.
  • FAILED: the program exited with an error; inspect its output log.
  • CANCELLED: the user or an administrator cancelled it.
  • PREEMPTED or a requeued scavenger job: best-effort work yielded to higher-priority work.

docs.title: Why is my job pending?
docs.text:
Pending is normal. Run squeue --me and inspect the reason. Resources means the requested shape is busy; Priority means other work is ahead; AssocGrpGRES commonly means an account or course-holder GPU cap is in use. squeue --me --start is an estimate, not a guarantee.

Sprocket’s Queue and Usage pages add current pressure, history, and evidence-qualified wait ranges.

docs.title: Can I SSH directly to a compute node?
docs.text: Only while you hold an allocation on that node. Start with salloc, find the assigned node using squeue --me, and then SSH to it. Without an allocation, connect to sprlab005 and submit work through Slurm.

docs.title: I need only CPUs. Do I still use Slurm?
docs.text:
Research accounts do:

salloc --cpus-per-task=8 --mem=32G --time=1:00:00

Course-only compute is GPU-budgeted and rejects CPU-only jobs. If a course assignment needs substantial CPU-only work, course staff must provide the intended workflow.

docs.title: Why is interactive research limited to an hour?
docs.text: Interactive research runs on the high-turnover debug partition. Use it to develop and diagnose, then move unattended or longer work to sbatch on main. A course assignment has its own wall-time ceiling and budget; always request only the interactive time needed.

docs.title: What is my account type?
docs.text: Sprocket’s Me and Course pages show the available role and course membership. Graduate and undergraduate research accounts use research QoS. A course-only account uses assignment budgets. A researcher enrolled in a course remains research by default and selects a course assignment account only for course work. See Accounts and access.

docs.title: What course account should I use?
docs.text: Copy --account=<assignment> from Sprocket’s Checkpoints page or run mybudget. When multiple assignments are open, the account is required. Do not guess a Slurm leaf account or copy another team’s value.

docs.title: How is course budget charged?
docs.text: Requested GPUs × requested wall minutes is held when the job is submitted. After completion, actual elapsed GPU-minutes become consumed and unused held time becomes free again. Pending and running team jobs share the same holder pool. See Course workflow.

docs.title: Why does my course budget look unavailable?
docs.text: Sprocket intentionally fails closed when queue or accounting evidence is missing or stale. Wait briefly and refresh. If it persists, send Support the assignment, command, approximate time, and displayed source health. Do not attempt to route around the course account.

docs.title: Can course assignments overlap?
docs.text: Yes. Each open assignment has a separate budget and account. Select which one pays for the job. The two-GPU holder/user ceiling spans assignments, so overlapping windows do not multiply concurrency.

docs.title: My team changed. What happens to jobs, budget, and submissions?
docs.text: An instructor previews and applies the exception in Sprocket. Consumed minutes, existing job holds, closed history, and artifacts remain with their original holder. Staff explicitly choose what happens to free budget. Open confirmations affected by membership may be invalidated so the resulting team confirms a coherent revision.

docs.title: How do we submit course work?
docs.text: Declare an allowed GitHub revision or a path inside your assigned course workspace in Checkpoints. Sprocket resolves GitHub input to an immutable commit and snapshots path input as an immutable ZFS revision. Path submissions receive an immediate structural result and, when configured by staff, an instructor verifier result. Review the exact revision; every required team member confirms it. Confirmation waits for trusted zero active jobs and closes the assignment window when final.

docs.title: How do I request a course extension or budget exception?
docs.text: Use Request an adjustment on the relevant checkpoint. Attach the required private evidence there, not to ordinary Support. Course staff decide the academic exception and Sprocket records the resulting window and budget change.

docs.title: Where do files live?
docs.text: Research homes are under /spr-storage/home/<username> with the account-type quota shown in Sprocket. Course-only personal work is under /course/<NetID> with a standard 10 GiB baseline; team workspaces normally provide 50 GiB under /course/groups/<course>/<team>. Published checkpoint policy can grow course allocations, and they do not shrink automatically. See Storage for the complete map.

docs.title: Can Slurm email me?
docs.text:
Yes:

sbatch --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL,TIME_LIMIT --mail-user=<netid> train.sh

A bare NetID goes to <netid>@illinois.edu. The sending address is not monitored for replies.

docs.title: Can I use more GPUs?
docs.text:
Research limits depend on QoS: 4 for normal or expedite, 2 for undergrad, and up to 8 for requeueable scavenger. Each node has two GPUs, so requests above two span nodes and need suitable distributed code.

Course jobs use one node and at most two GPUs. The checkpoint may allow only one, and the requested cost must fit the assignment budget.

docs.title: Can I use VS Code?
docs.text: Yes. Attach VS Code Remote-SSH to sprlab005, edit persistent files there, and submit jobs from its terminal. Do not depend on an editor attached to a temporary compute allocation. See VS Code.

docs.title: A login-host command feels throttled
docs.text: Ordinary users are capped at about eight CPUs on sprlab005 so one local process cannot starve everybody’s shell. Move heavy compilation, preprocessing, extraction, or training into a Slurm job.

docs.title: Where do I ask for help?
docs.text: Use Sprocket Support for technical failures and include exact commands, job IDs, times, and errors. Use Resource requests for reviewed research resources. Course assignment rules, grading, teams, and academic exceptions belong with course staff and the course adjustment flow.

docs.title: Using the Sprocket portal
docs.text: Sprocket is the shared control and information surface for the cluster. Public operational information is available without an account; personal, course, lab, and administrative views appear after sign-in according to role.

docs.title: Cluster information
docs.text:
• Home summarizes GPU capacity, running and pending work, active users, recent utilization, and the overall contention index.
  • Queue shows current jobs and explains whether GPU utilization is unavailable because a job is pending, CPU-only, or missing telemetry.
  • Usage combines current pressure with seven-day activity and evidence-qualified wait ranges for comparable one- and two-GPU jobs. Forecasts are estimates, not reservations or guarantees.
  • Monitor gives signed-in lab users detailed node, GPU, process, storage, and telemetry-source health.
  • Efficiency ranks lab users only after enough job and GPU evidence exists. It combines GPU activity, CPU and memory fit, and storage headroom; it is coaching evidence, not a performance grade.

docs.title: Your account
docs.text: The Me page shows identity and access information, SSH keys when portal management is enabled, personal job and usage history, and storage usage with threshold guidance. A value marked unavailable means Sprocket lacks fresh evidence; it is not treated as zero.

docs.title: Course workspace
docs.text:
Students receive Course → Getting started and Course → Checkpoints. Those pages show course access, storage conventions, open assignment accounts, budgets, deadlines, declarations, confirmations, and adjustment requests. TAs and instructors also receive the Staff console for rosters, teams, checkpoint publication, exceptions, and support.

See Course workflow before submitting course jobs.

docs.title: Operational communication
docs.text:
• Service status is the current health and maintenance view.
  • News carries announcements.
  • Changes records user-visible fixes and deployments.

When current behavior conflicts with an older message, check the latest service status and change entry, then report the discrepancy.

docs.title: Get help
docs.text:
• Support is for failures, questions, and course or infrastructure problems. Include the command, job ID, approximate time, and exact error when applicable.
  • Resource requests is for research storage, temporary deadline priority, project space, or another operational resource that needs review.
  • Course assignment policy, grading, teams, and academic exceptions route to course staff through the course-aware support and adjustment flows.

Do not attach medical or similarly sensitive evidence to an ordinary support report. Use the private checkpoint adjustment workflow designed for that material.

docs.title: Priority, capacity, and fair sharing
docs.text: The cluster serves research and supported courses on the same eight GPUs. Research is governed primarily by QoS and recent use. Course work is governed by assignment budgets plus scheduled course capacity. Neither policy automatically kills ordinary running research or course jobs; only best-effort scavenger work is automatically requeued.

docs.title: Research tiers
docs.text:
Tier Who Queue priority Batch wall time GPUs per user expedite Researcher with an active deadline grant 1000 24 hours 4 normal Graduate researcher, default 500 3 days 4 undergrad Undergraduate researcher, default 400 1 day 2 scavenger Any researcher, explicit best effort 1 1 day 8

Research users do not choose normal or undergrad; the account supplies the correct default. expedite is selectable only during an approved grant. scavenger is opt-in and batch-only.

Interactive research sessions are routed to debug, which has a one-hour cap and schedules ahead of pending batch work without preempting a running job. An interactive expedite session is the deadline exception and runs on main; interactive scavenger is rejected.

docs.title: Research fair sharing
docs.text:
Within a research tier, recent GPU-weighted usage affects queue order. The decay half-life is three days: usage matters most immediately and fades continuously rather than resetting on a particular day. A person who has used less recently generally moves ahead of a peer in the same tier.

QoS priority dominates fair share and age, so tiers do not invert. A normal job remains ahead of undergrad, and both remain ahead of scavenger, regardless of recent usage.

Reserved GPUs count even when utilization is low. This is deliberate: a GPU held idle is unavailable to everybody else. Request accurate resources and cancel abandoned jobs.

docs.title: Course tier
docs.text:
Course jobs use the shared course QoS at priority 200. They do not compete through the research normal, undergrad, expedite, or scavenger controls. Instead, three limits work together:

  1. Assignment budget: requested GPUs multiplied by wall time must fit the holder’s free GPU-minutes.
  2. Holder and user cap: no holder or course user can occupy more than two GPUs across overlapping assignments.
  3. Scheduled class capacity: course jobs attach to a Sprocket-owned reservation that bounds the class’s total GPU use for the current time window.

The initial capacity posture reserves up to two GPUs on weekdays from 07:00–18:00 Central and up to six GPUs on weekday nights and weekends. Administrators can adjust the schedule in Sprocket as course and research demand changes. Running jobs may cross a schedule boundary; the new cap controls additional starts rather than killing work already running.

Instructors set each checkpoint’s budget, GPU cap up to the two-GPU holder ceiling, wall-time ceiling, dates, and storage allowance. Those values appear on the student’s Checkpoints page and are more specific than this cluster-wide overview.

docs.title: Why reservations are used
docs.text:
The schedule preserves an intentional balance without making research and course users micromanage one another. During research-heavy daytime hours, most GPUs remain outside course capacity. Nights and weekends provide more course capacity. The posture can be tuned during the semester using observed contention.

Course jobs never use debug, and course-only students cannot escape into research policy. A dual-role researcher stays in research policy unless they explicitly select a course assignment account.

docs.title: Deadline research: expedite
docs.text:
For a genuine paper or demo deadline, submit a Resource request in Sprocket or use the lab’s established coordination channel. A grant is normally time-limited and automatically expires. Once approved:

sbatch --qos=expedite --gres=gpu:1 --time=24:00:00 train.sh

Expedite raises queue priority; it does not evict ordinary running work. It is not a course-budget extension.

docs.title: Best effort: scavenger
docs.text:
Restartable research work can use otherwise idle GPUs:

sbatch --qos=scavenger --gres=gpu:4 sweep.sh

Scavenger has the lowest priority and may be requeued when higher-priority work needs its resources. The job restarts from the beginning unless the program writes and restores checkpoints. It cannot run interactively and is not available to course jobs.

docs.title: Inspect queue position
docs.text:
squeue --me --start
sprio -l
sshare -l

Start times are estimates. Reservations, requested shape, higher-priority arrivals, and jobs ending earlier or later than requested can move them.

docs.title: Running jobs
docs.text:
Connect to sprlab005.csl.illinois.edu, request resources through Slurm, and let Slurm place the work on a compute node. The login host is not a compute node.

Research and course jobs route differently

The research examples below rely on the account’s default research policy. Course students must also select the assignment account shown in Sprocket; course-only accounts cannot submit unbudgeted research work. See Course workflow.

docs.title: Interactive or batch
docs.text:
• Interactive (salloc or standalone srun) is for development, debugging, and short tests where you need a shell.
  • Batch (sbatch) is for unattended training, sweeps, data preparation, and anything you want to leave running.

For research accounts, interactive work is routed to debug and capped at one hour. Batch work runs on main and follows the selected research tier’s wall-time limit. Course work always runs through the course gate on main; its assignment supplies the wall-time ceiling and budget.

docs.title: Short research session
docs.text:
salloc --gres=gpu:1 --time=1:00:00
squeue --me
ssh <assigned-node>

Each node has two GPUs, so a single-node request can use one or two. An interactive research request above one hour is trimmed to one hour. An explicit research interactive request for main is rejected; submit a batch job instead.

For CPU-only research work, leave off the GPU request:

salloc --cpus-per-task=8 --mem=32G --time=1:00:00

Course allocations require a GPU and an assignment account:

salloc --account=<assignment> --gres=gpu:1 --time=0:30:00

docs.title: Submit a batch job
docs.text:
Create a script with resource requests at the top:

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
#SBATCH --job-name=train
#SBATCH --mail-type=END,FAIL
#SBATCH --mail-user=<netid>

srun python train.py

Then submit and monitor it:

sbatch train.sh
squeue --me

For course work, add the assignment account to the script or command:

#SBATCH --account=<assignment>

Use the exact value from Sprocket. When several assignments are open, omitting it is rejected because Slurm cannot know which budget to charge.

docs.title: Resource defaults
docs.text:
If a GPU job does not specify CPU or memory, each GPU receives 32 Slurm CPUs (16 physical cores) and about 384 GB of memory. Two GPUs receive 64 Slurm CPUs and about 768 GB. A CPU-only research job with no CPU request receives 4 Slurm CPUs and about 48 GB.

Request explicit values only when the job needs something different:

sbatch --gres=gpu:1 --cpus-per-task=16 --mem=128G --time=6:00:00 train.sh

Over-requesting reduces placement options and, for course work, holds more assignment budget.

docs.title: Connect to an allocated node
docs.text:
After salloc starts, squeue --me shows the assigned node. SSH to that node:

ssh sprc01
nvidia-smi

The session joins the allocation and inherits its GPU, CPU, memory, and time limits. SSH to a compute node without an allocation is declined. Start tmux on the login host before salloc if a brief network interruption would otherwise lose an interactive shell.

docs.title: Watch and diagnose
docs.text:
squeue --me
squeue --me --start
scontrol show job <jobid>
sacct -j <jobid> --format=JobID,State,Elapsed,MaxRSS,ReqTRES

Pending is normal. The reason field explains whether the job is waiting for resources, priority, a reservation, or an account/QoS limit. Start times are estimates and become less reliable farther into the future.

Use Sprocket Queue and Usage for the same system at a glance.

docs.title: Stop or change work
docs.text:
scancel <jobid>
scancel --me

Cancel work you no longer need. For course jobs, changes that affect cost or placement require cancel-and-resubmit so the budget reservation stays correct. Harmless metadata and hold/release operations remain available.

docs.title: Email notifications
docs.text: Use --mail-type=BEGIN,END,FAIL,TIME_LIMIT and --mail-user=<netid>. A bare NetID is delivered to <netid>@illinois.edu. Messages come from “SPRC Cluster”; replies are not monitored.

docs.title: Research deadline and best-effort tiers
docs.text: Research users can request a temporary expedite grant for a genuine paper or demo deadline, or submit checkpointable batch work with --qos=scavenger to use idle capacity at the risk of requeue. These options do not apply to course jobs. See Priority, capacity, and fair sharing.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text: Storage depends on account type and purpose. Research users have shared home and research data tiers. Course-only students receive bounded course storage, and team checkpoints can add a shared team workspace.

docs.title: Research home — /spr-storage/home
docs.text:
A research home is mounted at /spr-storage/home/<username> on the login host and every compute node. It has an account-type quota and is appropriate for code, configuration, conda environments, and results you need to keep.

Check usage in Sprocket’s Me page and from the shell:

du -sh /spr-storage/home/<username>

Large datasets, shared project trees, model weights, and temporary high-I/O working sets belong on the tiers below.

docs.title: Course storage — /course
docs.text:
A course-only student receives a normal Unix home backed by its own ZFS dataset at /course/<NetID>, rather than a research home under /spr-storage/home. It starts with a 10 GiB allocation, mode 0700, and remains personal even after teams form. Both the dataset quota and referenced-data quota are set to the same boundary, so retained immutable submission snapshots cannot grow outside the approved allocation.

A team checkpoint can create a shared workspace at:

/course/groups/<course>/<team>

The standard team quota is 50 GB. Checkpoint policy can request more space, and reconciliation never lowers a live quota below current usage. Only current team members receive the team group identity. Team changes preserve existing bytes and history rather than silently moving or deleting data.

A researcher who is also enrolled in a course keeps the existing research UID and passwd home. The research home remains $HOME; Sprocket also provides an isolated /course/<NetID> personal coursework workspace for individual path submissions, plus the team workspace needed for team checkpoints. The course workspace does not create a second Unix identity or replace the research home.

docs.title: Projects — /projects
docs.text:
/projects is research group storage for shared code, source trees, package installations, and datasets containing many small files. Directories are group-owned and carry an aggregate project quota rather than a per-person quota. Request a project directory or membership through Resource requests.

Course students should not assume they can use /projects; use the course workspace unless course staff explicitly provide another location.

docs.title: Large files — /data
docs.text:
/data is for large single files such as checkpoints, archives, and compressed shards. Research users can organize their own directory, commonly /data/<username>, with a standard 50 GB per-user quota across files they own.

Course-only accounts should use assigned course storage unless course staff explicitly publish a course data location.

docs.title: Shared model cache — /huggingface
docs.text:
The SSD-backed /huggingface cache provides one warm copy of commonly used Hugging Face models. HF_HOME and HF_HUB_CACHE are configured cluster-wide, so ordinary transformers, datasets, and huggingface_hub use it automatically.

The cache is shared. Do not delete or rewrite another user’s cached material, and do not create duplicate model caches in personal home unless a reproducibility requirement genuinely needs one.

Course staff may publish a more specific course model-cache convention; follow that instruction when present.

docs.title: Fast working data — /fast-data
docs.text:
/fast-data is SSD-backed shared scratch for the hot working set of a running research job. It has a standard 100 GB per-user quota. Stage frequently read or written data there, run against the staged copy, copy durable results back, and clean up.

It is working space, not the only copy of an artifact. It is also shared across nodes, so performance can still vary under contention.

Course-only students should use it only when course staff explicitly authorize a workflow and location; course storage limits remain the default boundary.

docs.title: Quick placement guide
docs.text: Material Research account Course-only account Personal code and durable results /spr-storage/home/<username> /course/<NetID> Team code and shared results /projects/<project> /course/groups/<course>/<team> Large checkpoints or archives /data/<username> Assigned course or team workspace Shared Hugging Face models /huggingface Course-published cache convention Temporary hot working set /fast-data Only when course staff authorize it

docs.title: Quotas and requests
docs.text:
Sprocket’s Me page reports observed home usage and quota when fresh telemetry is available. An unavailable reading is not proof of unlimited space.

Research users request additional storage through Resource requests. Course checkpoint storage and team workspaces are instructor-configured; use course staff or Sprocket Support when the assigned space is missing or incorrect.

docs.title: VS Code
docs.text: Connect VS Code Remote-SSH to the login host, edit there, and submit compute through Slurm from the integrated terminal. This keeps the editor stable while compute allocations start and end independently.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
Use Remote-SSH: Connect to Host and select:

<username>@sprlab005.csl.illinois.edu

Open the persistent research or course workspace assigned to the account. Off campus, connect to the university VPN first.

docs.title: Run research compute
docs.text:
From the integrated terminal:

sbatch train.sh
squeue --me

The job runs on a compute node while logs and outputs appear in shared storage that VS Code can read from the login host.

docs.title: Run course compute
docs.text:
Copy the assignment account from Sprocket Checkpoints:

mybudget
sbatch --account=<assignment> train.sh

Keep the account, GPU request, and realistic time limit in the batch script so teammates and course staff can reproduce the submission.

docs.title: Why not attach the editor to a compute node?
docs.text:
A compute-node SSH session requires an active allocation and is bound to that job’s limits. Research interactive allocations normally end within an hour, and course allocations consume assignment budget while held. An editor attached to the login host does not require a compute allocation and survives between jobs.

For a short terminal debugging session, use salloc, then SSH to the assigned node. Keep the VS Code window on the login host unless there is a specific reason to attach an editor to the temporary allocation.

docs.title: Guardrails
docs.text:
• The login host has no GPU. nvidia-smi belongs inside an allocation.
  • Keep training, heavy preprocessing, and large builds off the login host.
  • A language server or editor task that becomes resource-heavy is still subject to the login-host CPU cap.
  • Manage SSH keys from Sprocket’s Me page when that feature is available for the account.

Use Sprocket Support for connection or key problems and include the Remote-SSH error log when possible.

docs.title: Workflows and file management
docs.text: Keep durable files on the storage assigned to your account, stage only the data that benefits from faster I/O, and make every batch job reproducible from a repository plus documented inputs.

docs.title: A reliable run
docs.text:
1. Keep source and durable inputs in persistent storage. Research code belongs in /home or /projects; large research artifacts belong in /data. Course work belongs in the personal or team path assigned under /course.
  2. Use the shared model cache. Hugging Face tools use /huggingface automatically. Course staff may publish a course-specific cache convention.
  3. Stage a hot working set only when useful. Research jobs can use /fast-data for repeated high-I/O access. Course students use only locations authorized by course staff.
  4. Run from a script. Record dependencies, resource requests, input paths, output paths, random seeds, and the immutable code revision.
  5. Copy results back and clean scratch. Temporary fast storage is not a durable artifact store.

Small jobs that read data once may gain nothing from staging. Avoid copying data simply because a faster tier exists.

docs.title: Research pattern
docs.text:
# prepare on the login host
git -C /projects/<project> rev-parse HEAD

# submit reproducibly
sbatch --gres=gpu:1 --time=12:00:00 train.sh

For benchmarking, put timed, repeatedly accessed data on /fast-data, repeat the measurement, record cluster conditions, and avoid interpreting a single shared-system run as a stable hardware limit.

Checkpoint long or restartable work. This makes failures cheaper and lets suitable research jobs use scavenger without restarting from the beginning after requeue.

docs.title: Course pattern
docs.text:
mybudget
sbatch --account=<assignment> --gres=gpu:1 --time=1:00:00 train.sh

Before launching, coordinate with teammates because pending and running jobs share the holder budget. Commit and push outputs needed for grading, then declare the repository reference in Sprocket. Sprocket resolves it to an immutable revision; every required team member reviews and confirms that exact revision.

Do not use a mutable branch name alone as your record of what ran. Save the commit hash, job ID, Slurm account, parameters, and relevant artifact paths.

docs.title: Keep the login host responsive
docs.text: Use sprlab005 for editors, source control, modest compilation, file organization, and submission. Each ordinary user is capped at about eight CPUs there. Training, large extraction, preprocessing, and heavy builds belong in Slurm jobs.

docs.title: File ownership and collaboration
docs.text:
• Use group-owned research project directories for lab collaboration.
  • Use the assigned course team directory for course collaboration.
  • Set reasonable group permissions; do not solve access problems with world-writable directories.
  • Never place credentials, private adjustment evidence, or secrets in a shared repository or team directory.

See Storage for paths and quotas. Use Sprocket Support for a broken mount or permission boundary and Resource requests for reviewed research capacity changes.
